products.name: Third-Party Application Patching with Intune — Commercial
products.short_description: A repeatable third-party patching program in Intune for the apps attackers target most — Chrome, Adobe, Zoom and more — via the Enterprise App Catalog and packaged updates with detection, supersedence, and rings. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Patch the apps attackers actually target — Chrome, Adobe, Zoom and more — automatically, from Intune

Windows Update keeps the OS current, but the software that gets exploited most — browsers, Adobe Reader, Java, Zoom, 7-Zip, and dozens of other third-party apps — quietly drifts out of date on every device. Each unpatched version is an open door. This solution gives you a repeatable third-party patching program in Intune: use the Enterprise App Catalog where available and a packaged update method elsewhere, with detection and supersedence so devices move to the current version automatically, deployed in rings.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — why third-party apps are the prime attack surface, the Enterprise App Catalog (catalog apps with auto-update) model, the packaged/superseded Win32 update method for everything else, and the ring-based update model.
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Intune, app inventory, Enterprise App Catalog availability, packaging tooling for non-catalog apps, detection method, maintenance windows) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.
  • Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: inventory installed third-party apps and versions, onboard catalog apps with auto-update, package and supersede non-catalog apps, set detection and assignment rings, schedule updates, then validate and expand.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — installed third-party app/version discovery, patch-state validation, an out-of-date exposure report across the fleet, safe remediation of stuck updates, and an update-ring group builder.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Your highest-risk third-party apps kept current automatically across the fleet — catalog apps auto-updating, everything else packaged and superseded, deployed in rings — proven on a pilot before you scale.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • TPP-Discovery.ps1 — inventory installed third-party applications and versions on this device
    • TPP-Remediation.ps1 — safely nudge a device whose third-party app update is stuck
    • TPP-Report.ps1 — fleet-wide out-of-date exposure for managed third-party apps (Microsoft Graph)
    • TPP-Set-UpdateRingTargeting.ps1 — build the Pilot/Broad update-ring groups for third-party patching
    • TPP-Validation.ps1 — validate that managed third-party apps on this device meet their target versions

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
